solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dastardly con destroyed police headquarters

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked and broken up, so its letters can be rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked swindle has been wrecked, apparently by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTLAND YARD is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the familiar name for the London Metropolitan Police base, so it is literally a police headquarters.

clue.text: Knocked around Northern Ireland and drove off

indicators.note: around says one word is wrapped about the outside of the other

blocks.note: to bash is to hit or knock
NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone was roughed up in Northern Ireland and then drove away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove off' reads as a motoring past tense, but here it is transitive: sent someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel them or send them away, which is what 'drove off' means as a transitive verb.

clue.text: Correct leaders of European directorate in triplicate

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so take the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic picture of EU directors issuing correct paperwork in three copies.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it and put its errors right, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Working in America getting billed regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so keep every other letter of the word

blocks.note: USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America
the first, third and fifth letters of billed

explanation.surface: Someone at work in the States is getting charged at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable is in working order and able to be put to use, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Transplant trees and let develop

indicators.note: to develop is to change and grow into a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: move your trees and let them grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To transplant a population is to move people and settle them somewhere new, which is to resettle them.

clue.text: Want thing by church

blocks.note: it is a pronoun standing for a thing
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone wants a particular item placed beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless longing or craving, so it is a noun meaning a want or desire.

clue.text: Start to cook tough vegetable

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of cook
tough and hard are synonyms

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: start cooking a vegetable that is stringy and tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green plant eaten as a cooked vegetable, an example of the category.

clue.text: Lieutenant protected by very thin shield

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded and guarded by it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: sheer fabric is very thin and fine
LT is the military abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An army officer is defended by only a flimsy shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a cover or refuge that protects, so it is a noun meaning a shield or protective screen.

clue.text: Single carpet moved into bedroom perhaps

indicators.note: things that are moved are shifted around, so the letters are placed differently

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone rug has been carried through into a bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a bedroom is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom is one example of a place where people lie down to sleep and recover, hence a place for repose.

clue.text: Counterpart merely returning washing machine

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word merely is read backwards

blocks.note: a twin is an exact counterpart or match
but can mean merely or only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Someone's double simply comes back home with a washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin tub is an older style of washing machine, common in Britain, with one drum for washing and another for spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is a type of domestic laundry appliance with two separate drums, so it is an example of a washing machine.

clue.text: Distinctive character of those moving last to first

indicators.note: the final letter is shifted round to the front of the word, rotating it by one place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of people whose personality shows as they come from behind to win.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values that marks out a group or culture.

clue.text: Repugnant sailor with house by river split

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
HO is the abbreviation for house
R is the abbreviation for river
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear apart

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a sailor's house beside a river has been torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent inspires loathing and disgust, which is the sense of repugnant.

clue.text: Just disagreeable head is missing

indicators.note: a word with no head has lost its first letter, so drop the opening one

blocks.note: frightful means very unpleasant or disagreeable

explanation.surface: A complaint that an unpleasant person in charge has gone absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like a mere adverb but is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful means legitimate or deserved, which is the adjective sense of just, as in a just claim.

clue.text: Cold greeting in Greek letter

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A frosty hello is written in Greek script.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second character of the Greek alphabet, written like an X.

clue.text: Prize pig beginning to destroy item of furniture

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a cup is a trophy awarded as a prize
a boar is a male pig
the opening letter of destroy

explanation.surface: An award-winning hog starts wrecking the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a cabinet with doors and shelves, an example of a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Druid oddly is no good

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, the first, third and fifth letters

blocks.note: letters one, three and five of Druid

explanation.surface: A verdict that a strange pagan priest is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that fails to work, so as an adjective it means useless or no good.

clue.text: Money private investigator gets initially finding pet

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take just the first letter of the word

blocks.note: a guinea is an old British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings
PI is the abbreviation for private investigator
the opening letter of gets

explanation.surface: A detective is paid and, at first, comes across a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is a small rodent commonly kept by children, an example of a household pet.

clue.text: Drink that is covering minute part of apron

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around the outside, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
M is the abbreviation for minute
the bib is the upper section of an apron covering the chest

explanation.surface: A quick drink is taken while wearing a tiny bit of an apron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny in the surface, but it is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, usually alcohol, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bit of lamb I threw in range

indicators.note: a bit of something is a portion of it, so the answer is a run of letters within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: Someone hurled a piece of lamb across the range in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests a cooker in this kitchen scene; it means scope.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit is the scope or extent of something's influence, which is one sense of range.

clue.text: Fish deep

blocks.note: first meaning: a spiny-finned fish, pronounced to rhyme with mass
second meaning: low in pitch, as of a voice, rhyming with base

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are spelt the same but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an edible fish and, as an adjective, describes a sound low in pitch.

clue.text: Predator in tavern immediately left

blocks.note: a bar is a place serving drinks, like a tavern
now means at once, immediately
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dangerous person in a pub has just walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn owl is a nocturnal bird of prey that hunts mice and voles, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Annoy king having a fortune but missing penny

indicators.note: missing means lacking something, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
a pile is informal for a large amount of money
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A rich monarch who is short of a single penny gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: PILE loses its P to leave ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to irritate or anger them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dirt bus dispersed causes upset

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered in all directions, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dust cart scattering muck makes people annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to unsettle or agitate them, which is what causing upset means.

clue.text: Poem disturbed Cyril

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of its settled state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name supplies the five letters

explanation.surface: A verse upset a man named Cyril.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, so it is a kind of poem.
